name: Earthjustice
mission: Founded in 1971, Earthjustice fights to preserve magnificent places and wildlife, protect people's health, advance clean energy, and combat climate change. As the premier nonprofit environmental law organization, we take on the biggest, most precedent-setting cases across the country. With more than 200 attorneys in 15 regional offices, we serve hundreds of public-interest clients, providing top-tier legal representation free of charge.
theoryOfChange: Earthjustice explicitly states its theory of change in relation to its work on clean energy, noting that 'if you force coal-fired power plants to enter the 20th century... coal power won't be able to compete economically with sources of energy that are genuinely clean.' Additionally, Earthjustice has adopted a 'justice framework' which was introduced in 2025 by the Community, Justice, and Impact (CJI) Department. This framework aims to drive strategic and operational alignment around the organization's values and mission to advance justice, serving as a strategic partner for impact assessment and analysis. The justice framework conceives of an 'Ecosystem of Justice' to achieve a democratic, multi-racial society that incorporates and serves all people and the planet. Earthjustice also publishes a 'Strategic Plan' and 'Program Report' that outline its goals and approach.

rich_narrative.summary: Founded in 1971, Earthjustice operates as a public interest environmental law firm using legal strategies to protect natural ecosystems and public health [4]. In FY2024, the organization managed <cite id="2">$139,607,013 in total revenue</cite> to fund strategic litigation, administrative advocacy, and policy efforts [2]. Earthjustice maintains <cite id="1">a 100/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite> [1]. The organization allocates a moderate share of its budget directly to core activities, reporting a <cite id="2">79.4% program expense ratio in FY2024</cite> [2]. Financial health remains steady, supported by low fundraising costs and a strong reserve base [1]. However, because the organization focuses on public interest environmental law rather than traditional faith-based relief, it demonstrates a lower alignment with specific Muslim donor priorities [4].
